newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK C.BANK SAYS TIGHT POLICY BRINGING RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK C.BANK SAYS TIGHT POLICY BRINGING RESULTS.

text.p: The Slovak central bank (NBS) on Thursday said its strict monetary policy measures, imposed gradually since last summer, were now bringing the desired positive results in money supply and credit expansion.
"I can say now that the policy measures are working in the way they were designed, they are reducing M2 growth and credit expansion," NBS Governor Vladimir Masar told journalists.
The NBS implemented a series of measures last summer to rein in rapidly growing credit expansion which was at the heart of fast growth in money supply.
The measures included increasing minimum reserves requirements for commercial banks and imposing special foreign exchange position measure to limit depositing of foreign funds in Slovak banks.

The NBS moved further in its restrictions at the beginning of this year, reacting to the expansive state budget spending plans, when it stopped fixing repo rate, which commercial banks often used as a last resort to refinance their activities.
The M2 money supply aggregate - the key NBS yardstick to assess monetary development - has gradually declined to 13.9 percent, year-on-year, growth in February from 19.5 percent last August.
In February 1996, M2 expansion was 21 percent year-on-year.
The overall amount of credits was 374.80 billion crowns at the end of last year, slighlty up from 354.10 billion crowns last summer when the NBS imposed the restrictive measures.
Masar said NBS measures helped curb credit expansion which, he said, now showed a positive trend.
The tight monetary policy created an acute liquidity shortage on the interbank market, pushing interest rates to record levels of above 26 percent several times this year.
Rates on the interbank market ranged from an average 15.79 percent for o/n funds to 18.28 percent for three-month money.
Masar said he was "not happy" with the current high interbank rates, but he also said that the central bank was not considering any change in rates at the moment.
